headline.text: Pohjois-Pohjanmaa lags nationally in crude curative treatment at 23.6% (95% CI 21.1–26.3; n=248/1050) versus 27.0% (4009/14873) across Finland.

details.text: The 95% confidence interval for Pohjois-Pohjanmaa's crude curative treatment share of 23.6% (95% CI 21.1–26.3; n=248/1050) excludes and lies below the national benchmark of 27.0% (4009/14873).

Because treatment categories overlap and a patient can receive several treatments, the county's crude life-prolonging share of 37.4% (95% CI 34.5–40.4; n=393/1050) has a 95% confidence interval that excludes and exceeds the national 30.4% (4522/14873), whereas crude symptomatic treatment at 38.8% (95% CI 35.9–41.7; n=407/1050) includes the national 39.5% (5871/14873).

Pohjois-Pohjanmaa's crude share of patients with a recorded MDT meeting is 1.1% (95% CI 0.7–2.0; n=12/1050), whose 95% confidence interval excludes the national 6.0% (893/14873), though MDT records measure recording practice rather than care because HILMO captures specialised procedures only from direct patient contacts.

In preliminary, unpublished national figures, lung cancer care in Finland takes an average of 155 days from initial symptoms to treatment, compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark, comprising 56 days of patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care.

headline.text: Public registry data show crude 12-month treatment shares with 95% confidence intervals, but lack county age-adjusted tables, stage for about 48% of patients, and pathway wait times.

details.text: The county table (Taulukko 11) reports crude shares that are not age-adjusted; county-level age-adjusted shares appear only in Kuva 16, where digitised national curative reference lines are 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women (±0.5 percentage points), with no digitised county value available here to test whether Pohjois-Pohjanmaa's gap holds after age adjustment.
As a separate limitation, crude county treatment shares cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of new patients in the report.

Pohjois-Pohjanmaa's crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 25.0% (95% CI 22.5–27.8; n=263/1050), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 27.5% (4089/14873) and mixes untreated patients with unrecorded treatment, while a journal article finding that HILMO diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types concerns diagnosis concordance only.

Public report data do not measure symptoms or referrals, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, imaging appears only indirectly as the clinical basis of diagnosis in approximately 20% of cases, and HILMO records whether specialist visits (93.6% nationally within 12 months) or treatments occurred within 12 months but not when.

headline.text: The team recommends tracking access times using THL 21/2016 definitions, standardising referral templates and diagnostic contacts, and publishing how completely stage, drug treatment, and MDT meetings are recorded.

details.text: Given Pohjois-Pohjanmaa's crude 1.1% (95% CI 0.7–2.0; n=12/1050) recorded MDT share versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally and about 48% missing stage nationally, the team recommends publishing per county how completely stage, drug treatment, and MDT meetings are recorded while Finland lacks a cancer quality registry and lung cancer data reporting remains incomplete.

Because the Health Care Act sets no maximum time for a cancer suspicion and national pathway monitoring is lacking, the team recommends reporting access times using THL Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers while the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation.

Supported by mentor insight that weak referrals receive lower urgency ratings and by varying local referral instructions, the team recommends a standard referral template, pulmonologist referral for persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray, and a named diagnostic-phase contact while the STM roadmap (measure 1.2.3) plans care-coordinator guidance by 2026–2028 for county adoption by 2029–2031.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.
rec:1.location: §1. Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact

rec:3.claim_text: Team recommendation 3: Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding. Publish, per county, how completely stage, drug treatment and MDT meetings are recorded. Read county ‘gaps’ in these fields as data-quality signals first.
rec:3.location: §3. Report recording completeness per county: stage, drug treatment, MDT coding
